On this system, the traditional SysV init startup scripts live in:

- **`/etc/init.d/`** (the actual init scripts)
- Runlevel symlink dirs (what runs at boot/shutdown): **`/etc/rc0.d/` … `/etc/rc6.d/`** and **`/etc/rcS.d/`**

There’s also a **`/etc/systemd/`** directory present (systemd units/config), but `/etc/init.d` + `/etc/rc*.d` are the classic “init scripts” locations.
[Sat 2026-05-09 06:47 UTC] Create a script that initiates a network connection upon boot

Create a SysV init script in **`/etc/init.d/`** and enable it via the **`/etc/rc*.d/`** runlevel links.

### 1) Script: `/etc/init.d/boot-net-connect`
```sh
#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          boot-net-connect
# Required-Start:    $network $remote_fs
# Required-Stop:     $network
# Default-Start:     2 3 4 5
# Default-Stop:      0 1 6
# Short-Description: Bring up a network connection at boot
### END INIT INFO

set -eu

IFACE="${IFACE:-eth0}"
LOGTAG="boot-net-connect"

do_start() {
  logger -t "$LOGTAG" "Starting: bringing up $IFACE via dhclient"
  if command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ip link set "$IFACE" up || true
  fi
  # Acquire/renew DHCP lease (change this to your connection command if needed)
  if command -v dhclient >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dhclient -v "$IFACE"
  else
    logger -t "$LOGTAG" "dhclient not found; install isc-dhcp-client or replace with your connection command"
    exit 1
  fi
  logger -t "$LOGTAG" "Done"
}

do_stop() {
  logger -t "$LOGTAG" "Stopping: releasing DHCP for $IFACE"
  if command -v dhclient >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dhclient -r "$IFACE" || true
  fi
  if command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ip link set "$IFACE" down || true
  fi
}

case "${1:-}" in
  start) do_start ;;
  stop) do_stop ;;
  restart|force-reload) do_stop || true; do_start ;;
  status) exit 0 ;;
  *) echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|restart|force-reload|status}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
```

### 2) Install + enable at boot
```sh
sudo install -m 0755 /etc/init.d/boot-net-connect /etc/init.d/boot-net-connect
sudo update-rc.d boot-net-connect defaults
```

### 3) Test now
```sh
sudo /etc/init.d/boot-net-connect start
```

If you tell me *what kind* of “network connection” you mean (DHCP on an interface, Wi‑Fi via wpa_supplicant, PPPoE, VPN like WireGuard/OpenVPN), I can tailor the `do_start()` command accordingly.
